Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.workspace

Class WorkspacePlugin

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.scenemanager.utils.workspace.WorkspacePlugin
All Implemented Interfaces:
SceneManagerPlugin
public class WorkspacePlugin extends Object implements SceneManagerPlugin
Multiple workspaces (virtual desktops) for the native 3D desktop: the plugin counterpart of the 2D/Swing desktop's WorkspaceModel + WorkspacePager pair, and the first window-management feature ported off the taskbar. GlassyTaskbar is not touched.

A workspace here is a partition of the open Frame3Ds: the plugin tracks frames through Frame3DAddedEvent/Frame3DRemovedEvent, assigns each to the workspace that is current when it opens, and shows or hides it through Component3D.setVisible(boolean) on every switch. The pure bookkeeping lives in WorkspaceRegistry (headless-testable); this class is only the scene-graph and event glue.

Why not the multi-AppContainer plumbing

SceneControl.setCurrentAppContainer was evaluated and rejected. It deliberately does not add a container to the scene graph (its own comment says the caller must, and SceneControl exposes no scene root to do it with), AppContainer.setEnabled only flips a boolean, getAppContainer leaves null slots that setCurrentAppContainer would then dereference, and — decisively — StandardAppContainer.initialize() registers global Frame3D listeners, including a to-front handler that migrates the frame into that container's main layout, with a comment warning that instantiating the container more than once duplicates those actions. A second workspace container would therefore pull frames back into the first. Partitioning the single container's frames is both smaller and correct; see WorkspaceRegistry for the full rationale.

Input

Switching is offered two ways. The HUD pager (a WorkspacePager3D in the top-left corner) is clickable — cell for direct switch, arrows to step. The keystrokes mirror the 2D desktop's ShortcutMap: Alt+Shift+Page Down/Page Up page through the workspaces and Alt+Shift+1..9 moves the front window. Ctrl+Alt+arrow is deliberately not bound because the host window manager grabs it in dev mode.

Keys arrive through a global KeyEvent3D listener on LgEventSource.ALL_SOURCES. This relies on the scene root already being a key event source — SceneManagerBase installs its own Ctrl+P handler there, which is what marks it — and, as PickEngine documents, a key event goes to the deepest key-event source under the pointer, so a keystroke typed into a focused text field of an application is delivered to that application. That is the same limitation the existing Ctrl+P binding has.

Following the front window

The taskbar's thumbnails are not workspace-aware (and must not be modified), so clicking one for a window on another workspace would otherwise "focus" an invisible window. The plugin therefore listens for Component3DToFrontEvent and switches to the workspace that window lives on, which makes the taskbar behave as a user expects.

getPluginRoot() returns null: the pager is parented to the HUD layer rather than the scene root, so it inherits the layer's perspective-compensated front pose. When DesktopHudPlugin is not running the pager is skipped with a warning, but the registry and the keystrokes still work.
